results.title: Eagles out of finals race
results.description: The Eagles are out of the finals race after they lost to the Thunder on Saturday. The Eagles are out of the finals race after they lost to the Thunder on Saturday. Coach of Warrack, Kyle George, described the situation as "unbelievably disappointing". Buoyed by what Thunder's coaching director Jake Bridges described as a "magic highlight" for the club, Simon Clugston's 250th club game, Bridges' side secured their own finals place with the 13.15 (93) to 7.11 (53) win. The result means the final five teams to contest finals are now settled, with Ararat, the Saints, Stawell, Nhill and Thunder all advancing, although the exact positions could change still. The Eagles got off to a fast start and were up by 11 points at the end of the first quarter, but encouraged by the message from Bridges at the break, the Thunder held the advantage by five points at half-time. A 5.5 quarter, compared to the opposition's 2.0, meant Southern Mallee were able to take a 28-point lead into the final quarter, before the Thunder continued on their way and recorded the 40-point win. For the losing side, Ben Hanna and Billy Stokes battled hard all day, while Sam Hanna contributed a couple of majors. For the home side and winners, better players included Jai Kennealy and William Page, while Kai Sheers was impressive in the forward line with four goals. "We started well, but just dropped off for 15 minutes and they scored on us," George lamented. "Uncontested marks killed us, and the Thunder definitely worked harder in the third." While George said some players stood up - including the likes of Ben Hanna in and under, along with Samuel Callins and Stokes, he was still disappointed in the loss. "We need to find that killer instinct fast," he concluded.
